metadata.title: Perceived teacher support, self-concept, enjoyment and achievement in reading: A multilevel mediation model based on PISA 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 mainland China data with a two-stage stratified sampling design (schools sampled first, then students within schools). The authors report that the sample was weighted to represent 992,302 15-year-old students in mainland China, indicating application of PISA sampling weights in estimation. The analysis is multilevel (students nested within schools) and therefore weights are relevant for producing population-representative estimates under the complex design. The manuscript does not report a specific weight variable name or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the exact implementation details in the software are not fully transparent.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analyses were conducted on mainland China PISA 2018 data for the target population of 15-year-old students. The sampling followed PISA’s two-stage stratified procedure: 362 schools were selected from Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang provinces, and up to 35 students per school were randomly selected, yielding 12,058 students. The study uses the full PISA reading literacy assessment as the reading literacy outcome. For continuous variables, missing data were handled using EM (expectation-maximization) as reported in the analysis section; no additional grade- or school-type restrictions are described beyond the PISA 15-year-old target population.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel mediation (Mplus): Step 1 effect of student-level teacher support on reading literacy: B=5.511, SE=1.177, p<0.001. Step 1 effect of school-level teacher support on reading literacy: B=15.883, SE=16.102, p>0.05. Step 4 (mediators included): reading enjoyment B=23.999, SE=1.584, p<0.001; reading self-concept B=18.073, SE=2.297, p<0.001. With mediators, direct effects: student-level teacher support B=1.668, SE=1.200, p=0.164; school-level teacher support B=15.465, SE=16.041, p=0.335. Model fit reported: H0=-81,876.697; AIC=163,807.395; BIC=164,006.827.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading (15-year-olds, China) the study leveraged student-perceived teacher support (at student and school levels) together with gender and socioeconomic status to model reading literacy, finding that student-level teacher support had a significant positive association with reading literacy while school-level teacher support did not. When reading enjoyment and reading self-concept were included as mediators, both mediators showed significant positive associations with reading literacy and the direct associations of teacher support with reading literacy became non-significant, indicating mediation. This indicates that strengthening classroom-level teacher support may improve reading achievement primarily by enhancing students’ reading enjoyment and reading self-concept, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes mainland China PISA 2018 data for 15-year-old students (N=12,058; 362 schools) to test a multilevel mediation model grounded in expectancy-value theory. The outcome is reading literacy from the PISA 2018 reading assessment, and the mediators are reading enjoyment and reading self-concept measured via Likert scales. The authors estimate multilevel mediation in Mplus and handle missing continuous variables using EM; reading literacy parameters are combined across the ten plausible-value datasets using Rubin’s combination rules. In the mediation results, student-level perceived teacher support significantly predicts reading literacy (B=5.511, SE=1.177, p<0.001), but school-level teacher support does not (p>0.05). Reading enjoyment (B=23.999, SE=1.584, p<0.001) and reading self-concept (B=18.073, SE=2.297, p<0.001) remain significant when included, while direct teacher-support effects become non-significant. Limitations include the cross-sectional nature of PISA and the fact that the analysis is mediation modeling rather than ML prediction.
